title: "CellCharterR reproduction of the CellCharter CODEX mouse-spleen tutorial"
author: "CellCharterR checkpointed workflow"
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC', tz = 'UTC')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
    number_sections: true
    code_folding: show
    df_print: paged
params:
  result_dir: null
---

```{r setup, echo=TRUE, message=TRUE, warning=TRUE}
# Every chunk is deliberately visible: this report is an auditable view of
# checkpointed results, not a hidden re-analysis of the tutorial data.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE,
  fig.align = "center", fig.retina = 2,
  dev.args = list(pointsize = 16)
)

project_root <- if (file.exists(file.path(getwd(), "DESCRIPTION"))) {
  getwd()
} else if (file.exists(file.path(dirname(getwd()), "DESCRIPTION"))) {
  dirname(getwd())
} else {
  stop(
    "Render from the CellCharterR repository root (or its reports/ directory). ",
    "The project DESCRIPTION file could not be located.", call. = FALSE
  )
}

result_dir <- params$result_dir
if (is.null(result_dir) || length(result_dir) != 1L || !nzchar(result_dir)) {
  result_dir <- file.path(project_root, "results", "codex_mouse_spleen")
}
result_dir <- normalizePath(result_dir, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)

# These are the durable artifacts needed to substantiate every primary result
# shown below. Report rendering never silently regenerates or substitutes them.
artifact_paths <- c(
  representation = file.path(result_dir, "representation", "codex_sce.rds"),
  graph_manifest = file.path(result_dir, "graph", "graph_manifest.rds"),
  aggregation_manifest = file.path(result_dir, "aggregation_pinned_global", "aggregation_manifest.rds"),
  aggregation_parity = file.path(result_dir, "aggregation_pinned_global", "python_r_parity.rds"),
  published_aggregation_parity = file.path(
    result_dir, "aggregation_pinned_global", "published_graph_python_r_parity.rds"
  ),
  python_gmm_fixture = file.path(project_root, "inst", "extdata", "python_gmm_k11_fixture.rds"),
  autok = file.path(result_dir, "autok_pinned_global", "autok_result.rds"),
  selected_labels = file.path(result_dir, "selected", "selected_labels.rds"),
  selected_model = file.path(result_dir, "selected", "selected_model.rds"),
  k11_labels = file.path(result_dir, "selected", "tutorial_sensitivity_k11_labels.rds"),
  downstream_manifest = file.path(result_dir, "downstream", "downstream_manifest.rds"),
  report_input = file.path(result_dir, "downstream", "report_input.rds"),
  cell_type_enrichment = file.path(result_dir, "downstream", "cell_type_enrichment.rds"),
  neighborhood_enrichment = file.path(
    result_dir, "downstream", "condition_neighborhood_enrichment.rds"
  ),
  differential = file.path(
    result_dir, "downstream", "BALBc_vs_MRL_differential_neighborhood.rds"
  ),
  k11_agreement = file.path(
    result_dir, "downstream", "tutorial_sensitivity_k11_reference_agreement.rds"
  )
)
missing_artifacts <- artifact_paths[!file.exists(artifact_paths)]
if (length(missing_artifacts)) {
  stop(
    "The CODEX report cannot be rendered because required checkpoint(s) are absent:\n  - ",
    paste(missing_artifacts, collapse = "\n  - "),
    "\nRegenerate/resume them from the repository root with:\n",
    "  Rscript scripts/run_codex_mouse_spleen.R\n",
    "or set CODEX_RESULTS_DIR to the completed checkpoint directory.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

sce <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["representation"]])
graph_manifest <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["graph_manifest"]])
aggregation_manifest <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["aggregation_manifest"]])
aggregation_parity <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["aggregation_parity"]])
published_aggregation_parity <- readRDS(
  artifact_paths[["published_aggregation_parity"]]
)
python_gmm_fixture <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["python_gmm_fixture"]])
autok <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["autok"]])
selected <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["selected_labels"]])
k11_selected <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["k11_labels"]])
downstream_manifest <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["downstream_manifest"]])
report_input <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["report_input"]])
cell_type_enrichment <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["cell_type_enrichment"]])
condition_nhood <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["neighborhood_enrichment"]])
differential <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["differential"]])
k11_agreement <- readRDS(artifact_paths[["k11_agreement"]])

if (!inherits(autok, "cellcharter_autok")) {
  stop("The AutoK checkpoint is not a `cellcharter_autok` result; rerun the AutoK stage.")
}
if (is.na(autok$best_k) || !identical(as.integer(selected$k), as.integer(autok$best_k))) {
  stop("The selected-label checkpoint does not match the R-selected AutoK result.")
}
if (!identical(as.integer(k11_selected$k), 11L)) {
  stop("The tutorial sensitivity checkpoint is not labelled K = 11.")
}
if (nrow(report_input) != length(selected$labels) ||
    nrow(report_input) != length(k11_selected$labels)) {
  stop("Map rows and selected label vectors differ in length; regenerate downstream checkpoints.")
}
if (!identical(as.integer(downstream_manifest$selected_k), as.integer(selected$k))) {
  stop("The downstream manifest was produced for a different selected K.")
}
if (!identical(as.integer(differential$params$n_perms), 100L)) {
  stop(
    "Tutorial parity requires n_perms = 100, but the differential checkpoint records ",
    differential$params$n_perms, ". Rerun with CODEX_N_PERMS=100."
  )
}
if (!identical(as.character(differential$params$condition_groups), c("BALBc", "MRL"))) {
  stop("The differential checkpoint must compare BALBc versus MRL in that order.")
}

workflow_metadata <- S4Vectors::metadata(sce)$CellCharterR
if (is.null(workflow_metadata)) {
  workflow_metadata <- S4Vectors::metadata(sce)$rCellCharter
}
if (is.null(workflow_metadata$reference) || is.null(workflow_metadata$inputs) ||
    is.null(workflow_metadata$parameters)) {
  stop("The representation checkpoint lacks required CellCharterR provenance metadata.")
}

format_value <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || !length(x)) return(NA_character_)
  if (inherits(x, "package_version")) return(as.character(x))
  paste(as.character(x), collapse = ", ")
}

list_table <- function(x, field_name = "field", value_name = "value") {
  data.frame(
    field = names(x),
    value = vapply(x, format_value, character(1)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    check.names = FALSE
  ) |>
    stats::setNames(c(field_name, value_name))
}

checkpoint_table <- data.frame(
  artifact = names(artifact_paths),
  path = unname(artifact_paths),
  size_mb = round(file.info(artifact_paths)$size / 1024^2, 3),
  modified_utc = format(file.info(artifact_paths)$mtime, tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE),
  row.names = NULL,
  check.names = FALSE
)

plot_matrix <- function(x, main, diverging = FALSE, digits = 3L) {
  x <- as.matrix(x)
  if (!length(x) || !is.numeric(x)) stop("A plotted result matrix must be non-empty and numeric.")
  finite_values <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (!length(finite_values)) stop("Matrix `", main, "` has no finite values to plot.")
  finite_range <- range(finite_values)
  plotted <- x
  plotted[is.infinite(plotted) & plotted < 0] <- finite_range[[1L]]
  plotted[is.infinite(plotted) & plotted > 0] <- finite_range[[2L]]
  if (diverging) {
    limit <- max(abs(finite_values))
    if (limit == 0) limit <- 1
    zlim <- c(-limit, limit)
    palette <- grDevices::hcl.colors(101L, "Blue-Red 3", rev = TRUE)
  } else {
    zlim <- finite_range
    if (zlim[[1L]] == zlim[[2L]]) zlim <- zlim + c(-0.5, 0.5)
    palette <- grDevices::hcl.colors(101L, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE)
  }
  old_par <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit({
    graphics::layout(1)
    graphics::par(old_par)
  })
  graphics::layout(matrix(c(1L, 2L), nrow = 1L), widths = c(10, 1.2))
  graphics::par(
    mar = c(max(6, 0.42 * max(nchar(colnames(x))) + 2),
            max(6, 0.22 * max(nchar(rownames(x))) + 2), 4, 2)
  )
  graphics::image(
    x = seq_len(ncol(plotted)), y = seq_len(nrow(plotted)), z = t(plotted),
    col = palette, zlim = zlim, axes = FALSE, xlab = "target domain",
    ylab = "source / cell type", main = main, useRaster = TRUE
  )
  graphics::axis(1, at = seq_len(ncol(x)), labels = colnames(x), las = 2,
                 cex.axis = 1)
  graphics::axis(2, at = seq_len(nrow(x)), labels = rownames(x), las = 2,
                 cex.axis = 1)
  graphics::box()

  # Draw a compact value scale using base graphics, avoiding an extra report
  # dependency solely for heat-map legends.
  key_values <- seq(zlim[[1L]], zlim[[2L]], length.out = 101L)
  graphics::par(mar = c(6, 0.5, 4, 4))
  graphics::image(
    x = 1, y = key_values, z = matrix(key_values, nrow = 1L),
    col = palette, zlim = zlim, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
    useRaster = TRUE
  )
  graphics::axis(4, at = pretty(zlim, n = 5L), las = 2, cex.axis = 1)
  graphics::box()
  invisible(round(zlim, digits))
}

plot_sample_grid <- function(data, domain, title) {
  samples <- unique(as.character(data$sample))
  n_columns <- min(4L, length(samples))
  n_rows <- ceiling(length(samples) / n_columns)
  domain <- factor(domain, levels = sort(unique(as.integer(as.character(domain)))))
  palette <- grDevices::hcl.colors(nlevels(domain), "Dynamic")
  symbols <- rep(c(16, 17, 15, 18, 3, 4, 8, 1, 2, 6, 0),
                 length.out = nlevels(domain))
  old_par <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(graphics::par(old_par))
  graphics::par(
    mfrow = c(n_rows, n_columns), mar = c(1.2, 1.2, 2.1, 0.5),
    oma = c(0, 0, 3, 0)
  )
  for (sample_id in samples) {
    keep <- as.character(data$sample) == sample_id
    point_size <- max(0.08, min(0.55, 2500 / sum(keep)))
    graphics::plot(
      data$x[keep], data$y[keep], asp = 1, axes = FALSE,
      xlab = "", ylab = "", pch = symbols[as.integer(domain[keep])], cex = point_size,
      col = palette[as.integer(domain[keep])], main = sample_id, cex.main = 1
    )
    graphics::box(col = "grey70")
  }
  for (unused in seq_len(n_rows * n_columns - length(samples))) graphics::plot.new()
  graphics::mtext(title, outer = TRUE, side = 3, line = 1, font = 2)
  attr(palette, "pch") <- symbols
  invisible(palette)
}
```

# Scope and interpretation

This report reproduces the **downstream** CellCharter CODEX mouse-spleen
workflow in R from the immutable official trVAE representation. The primary
path follows the pinned CellCharter 0.2.0 source, including its single global
99th-percentile link cutoff, and uses the number of spatial domains independently
selected by the R AutoK run. It does not claim end-to-end equivalence for
representation learning, and it does not substitute a PCA embedding for the
official trVAE input.

The primary R-selected result in this checkpoint is **K =
`r selected$k`**. The later K = 11 section is a tutorial-matched sensitivity
analysis only.

# Checkpoint inventory

```{r checkpoint-inventory, echo=TRUE}
knitr::kable(
  checkpoint_table,
  caption = paste("Durable report inputs under", result_dir)
)
```

# Provenance and parameters

## Pinned Python reference

```{r pinned-reference, echo=TRUE}
reference_table <- list_table(
  workflow_metadata$reference,
  field_name = "reference component",
  value_name = "pinned version or commit"
)
knitr::kable(reference_table, caption = "Authoritative parity reference")
```

The implementation target is CellCharter 0.2.0 at commit
`r workflow_metadata$reference$cellcharter_commit`, with PyCave rather than the
TorchGMM backend used by newer CellCharter releases.

The released Python artifacts do not declare the RNG seeds used for their
individual PyCave fits, so exact seed-for-seed replay of those artifacts is not
claimed. This R analysis predeclares base seed `r autok$seed`; repeat `i` uses
`base seed + i - 1` for every fitted K, and every fit artifact records its run
and seed. The best-fit table below exposes the retained seed for each K.

## Graph and aggregation checks

The R-native Qhull graphs were constructed independently within physical
samples, with no cross-sample edges. The pinned CellCharter 0.2.0 function
computes one global 99th-percentile cutoff across the combined sample-local
graph, and that is the primary analysis below. The released H5AD instead
contains a graph trimmed independently at the 99th percentile within each
sample. Repeating those per-sample cutoffs in R reproduces the published
adjacency edge-for-edge. Both results are checkpointed below: the global graph
for source-faithful primary inference, and the per-sample graph as a published-
artifact parity result.


## Pinned PyCave GMM prediction parity

The permanent fixture applies the official PyCave 3.2.1 K = 11 parameters to
512 deterministic rows of the exact released `X_cellcharter` matrix. Expected
labels are computed with PyCave's pinned row-vector precision-Cholesky formula;
the package test requires R's bounded-memory predictor to match every label.
This validates model deserialization and prediction mathematics, but it does
not claim that independently initialized EM fits must converge to the same
local optimum.

```{r python-gmm-prediction-parity, echo=TRUE}
python_gmm_parity_summary <- data.frame(
  field = c(
    "fixture rows", "features", "components", "reference backend",
    "CellCharter commit", "PyCave commit", "required prediction agreement",
    "official model versus released H5AD labels (FMI)"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(python_gmm_fixture$x), ncol(python_gmm_fixture$x),
    python_gmm_fixture$model$n_clusters,
    python_gmm_fixture$provenance$backend,
    python_gmm_fixture$provenance$cellcharter_commit,
    python_gmm_fixture$provenance$pycave_commit,
    python_gmm_fixture$provenance$expected_agreement,
    signif(python_gmm_fixture$published_label_fmi, 6)
  )
)
knitr::kable(
  python_gmm_parity_summary,
  caption = "Pinned Python-model prediction fixture (verified by package tests)"
)
```

# AutoK stability and primary K selection

AutoK fitted the expanded neighboring-K grid repeatedly, compared neighboring
solutions with the Fowlkes--Mallows score, and retained the lowest-negative-
log-likelihood fit for each K. The declared candidate range, run cap, and
convergence tolerance were fixed before the analysis.

```{r autok-summary, echo=TRUE}
autok_summary <- data.frame(
  field = c(
    "reference version", "reference commit", "declared candidate K",
    "expanded fitted K", "max runs", "runs completed", "convergence tolerance",
    "converged", "base seed", "R-selected K"
  ),
  value = c(
    autok$reference_version,
    autok$reference_commit,
    paste(range(autok$requested_k), collapse = " through "),
    paste(range(autok$fit_k), collapse = " through "),
    autok$max_runs,
    autok$runs_completed,
    autok$convergence_tol,
    autok$converged,
    autok$seed,
    autok$best_k
  )
)
knitr::kable(autok_summary, caption = "AutoK configuration and outcome")

stability_diagnostic <- cellcharter_autok_stability_data(
  autok, k_range = 1:20, highlight_k = c(4L, 11L)
)
stability_table <- stability_diagnostic$summary
knitr::kable(
  stability_table,
  digits = 5,
  caption = "Mean mirrored neighboring-K stability; maximum selects primary K"
)
```


# Cell-type enrichment for the primary result

Before this analysis, the detailed annotations are collapsed to the tutorial's
`cell_type_reduced` categories (including combined DC, stroma, and other
groups). Observed values are within-domain reduced-cell-type proportions. Expected values are
the cohort-wide cell-type proportions repeated for each domain. The reported
enrichment is `log2(observed / expected)`, matching the pinned CellCharter
observed-versus-expected analysis; it is not a simple composition table.
For visualization only, infinite enrichment values are clipped to the nearest
finite endpoint of the color scale; the checkpoint itself remains unchanged.

```{r cell-type-observed, echo=TRUE, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, fig.alt="Heatmap of observed reduced-cell-type proportions within primary domains"}
plot_matrix(
  cell_type_enrichment$observed,
  "Observed reduced-cell-type proportion within each primary domain"
)
```

```{r cell-type-expected, echo=TRUE, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, fig.alt="Heatmap of expected cohort-wide reduced-cell-type proportions"}

```

```{r cell-type-enrichment-parameters, echo=TRUE}
)
```

# Asymmetric neighborhood enrichment by condition

Rows are source domains and columns are target domains. The statistic is
directional: source-to-target enrichment need not equal target-to-source
enrichment. Same-domain links are excluded, leaving the diagonal undefined.
BALBc and MRL are calculated separately with the pinned analytical expectation.

```{r condition-neighborhood-enrichment, echo=TRUE, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, fig.alt="Condition-specific observed, expected, and directed neighborhood-enrichment heatmaps for BALBc and MRL"}
required_conditions <- c("BALBc", "MRL")
if (!all(required_conditions %in% names(condition_nhood))) {
  stop("The neighborhood checkpoint must contain separate BALBc and MRL results.")
}
for (condition_name in required_conditions) {
  result <- condition_nhood[[condition_name]]
  plot_matrix(
    result$observed,
    paste(condition_name, "observed directed inter-domain proportions")
  )
  plot_matrix(
    result$expected,
    paste(condition_name, "analytical expected directed proportions")
  )
  plot_matrix(
    result$enrichment,
    paste(condition_name, "asymmetric neighborhood enrichment"),
    diverging = TRUE
  )
}
```

```{r condition-neighborhood-parameters, echo=TRUE}
condition_parameter_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(required_conditions, function(condition_name) {
  data.frame(
    condition = condition_name,
    list_table(condition_nhood[[condition_name]]$params),
    row.names = NULL,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(
  condition_parameter_table,
  caption = "Condition-specific neighborhood-enrichment parameters"
)
```

# BALBc versus MRL differential neighborhood enrichment

The differential effect is BALBc enrichment minus MRL enrichment. Condition
labels are permuted at the sample/library level, never at the cell level. The
checkpoint uses exactly **100 permutations**, the sample as library unit, and
the CellCharter 0.2.0 directional empirical-tail convention.

```{r differential-parameters, echo=TRUE}
knitr::kable(
  list_table(
    differential$params,
    field_name = "differential parameter",
    value_name = "recorded value"
  ),
  caption = "BALBc-versus-MRL differential test parameters"
)
```

```{r differential-effect, echo=TRUE, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, fig.alt="Differential directed neighborhood enrichment, BALBc minus MRL"}
plot_matrix(
  differential$effect,
  "Differential asymmetric enrichment: BALBc minus MRL",
  diverging = TRUE
)
```

```{r differential-permutation-counts, echo=TRUE, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, fig.alt="Directional extreme-null permutation counts for domain pairs"}
plot_matrix(
  differential$permutation_counts,
  "Directional extreme-null permutation counts (n = 100)"
)
```

```{r differential-pvalues, echo=TRUE, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, fig.alt="Unadjusted directional empirical p-values for domain pairs"}
plot_matrix(
  differential$pvalue,
  "Unadjusted directional empirical p-values"
)
```

```{r differential-leading-results, echo=TRUE}
off_diagonal <- row(differential$effect) != col(differential$effect)
finite_test <- off_diagonal & is.finite(differential$effect) & is.finite(differential$pvalue)
leading <- data.frame(
  source_domain = rownames(differential$effect)[row(differential$effect)[finite_test]],
  target_domain = colnames(differential$effect)[col(differential$effect)[finite_test]],
  effect_BALBc_minus_MRL = differential$effect[finite_test],
  permutation_count = differential$permutation_counts[finite_test],
  empirical_pvalue = differential$pvalue[finite_test]
)
leading <- leading[order(leading$empirical_pvalue, -abs(leading$effect_BALBc_minus_MRL)), ]
knitr::kable(
  utils::head(leading, 25L),
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Top 25 directed domain pairs ordered by empirical p-value and effect magnitude"
)
```

# Tutorial-matched K = 11 sensitivity analysis (not primary)

This section does **not** replace the independently R-selected K =
`r selected$k` result. It shows the lowest-negative-log-likelihood K = 11 fit
only to facilitate visual comparison with the published tutorial convention.
No K = 11 enrichment or proximity statistic is presented as a primary result.

# Limitations

- The official fixed trVAE embedding is treated as immutable input. This report
  therefore tests downstream graph, aggregation, AutoK, GMM, enrichment, and
  proximity parity; it does not claim that R reproduced trVAE training.
- The published H5AD used per-sample link cutoffs, while the pinned CellCharter
  0.2.0 source called by its tutorial applies one global cutoff. The primary
  analysis follows the pinned source and therefore is not expected to equal the
  released 40-dimensional aggregate. The report shows that discrepancy
  explicitly. A separate R per-sample reconstruction matches the published
  adjacency edge-for-edge and its aggregation matches the released artifact.
- The primary maps and statistics use the R-selected K. K = 11 is isolated as a
  tutorial-matched sensitivity fit and is not evidence for independent K
  selection.
- Domain identifiers are label-permutation dependent and have no ordinal
  meaning. Biological interpretation requires inspecting their cell-type and
  spatial context.
- Neighborhood enrichment is asymmetric and excludes within-domain edges. Its
  expected values follow the pinned CellCharter 0.2.0 analytical definition.
- Differential inference uses samples as libraries and exactly 100
  permutations. Thus empirical p-values have coarse resolution; they use the
  pinned directional convention, have no +1 correction, and are unadjusted for
  multiple testing.
- Separate tissue sections are displayed as separate panels. Their raw spatial
  coordinates are not a registered common coordinate system.
- This document reads durable checkpoints and does not refit models. A stale or
  mixed checkpoint bundle is rejected by the consistency checks in the visible
  setup chunk.
